notes: Standalone example for a Proxmox VE node: each guest's newest backup on every backup storage, as text. The built-in sensor also reads the guests' network cards, which backup jobs cover them, verification state and the last vzdump task.

commands.linux:
# Standalone example (Proxmox VE node): newest backup per guest per storage, as text.
command -v pvesh >/dev/null || { echo 'not a Proxmox VE node'; exit 0; }
node=$(hostname -s)
for s in $(pvesh get /nodes/$node/storage --content backup --output-format json | grep -o '"storage":"[^"]*"' | cut -d'"' -f4); do
  pvesh get /nodes/$node/storage/$s/content --content backup --output-format json 2>/dev/null \
    | tr '{' '\n' | grep -o '"ctime":[0-9]*.*"vmid":[0-9]*' | sed -E 's/"ctime":([0-9]+).*"vmid":([0-9]+)/\2 \1/' \
    | sort -k1,1n -k2,2nr | awk -v s="$s" '!seen[$1]++ { printf "%s vmid %s: %s\n", s, $1, strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", $2) }'
done
commands.darwin:
# Backups are read on Proxmox VE nodes only; a Mac reports nothing.
echo 'not a Proxmox VE node'
commands.windows:
# Backups are read on Proxmox VE nodes only; Windows reports nothing.
'not a Proxmox VE node'
